subject: Game Theory
title: The Gibbard-Satterthwaite Theorem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Gibbard-Satterthwaite Theorem.

hook.text: You prefer candidate A but vote for B to prevent C from winning. This strategic voting plagues every election.

buildup.text: Tactical voting means reporting false preferences to manipulate the outcome. It's rational but undermines democracy.

discovery.text: Gibbard and Satterthwaite proved: every non-dictatorial voting system with 3+ options is vulnerable to manipulation.

twist.text: No system design, however clever, can make honest voting always optimal. Strategic manipulation can't be designed away.

climax.text: This doesn't mean all systems are equal. Some resist manipulation better. Mechanism design seeks the most robust ones.

punchline.text: Perfect honesty in voting is mathematically impossible.

quiz.question: What does the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem prove?
options: Every voting system with 3+ options can be strategically manipulated
